correctness.rationale: Enumerating all balanced four-mers gives exactly 96, 52 reverse-complement orbits with 8 fixed and 44 admissible two-member orbits. A 44-vertex deletion-shadow conflict graph has 344 edges. Fourteen explicit conflict cliques from certificate.json cover each vertex at least twice (36 with multiplicity 2 and eight with 3); a deletion-compatible independent set therefore has size ≤7, and seven explicit pairs realize it, giving 14 DNA words. Independent increasing-index enumeration of all compatible seven-orbit subsets yields exactly 20, and a full 16-action group calculation gives orbit sizes 4,4,4,8. Every seven-set was independently checked maximal, so no eight-set exists; this is a complete finite certificate, not merely a solver result.

value.rationale: GC balance, reverse-complement closure, avoidance of self-complement strands, and single-deletion correction are natural simultaneous DNA storage constraints. Their exact feasible maximum and complete 20-solution equality classification constitute an independently checkable finite extremal coding fact not implied by unrestricted or Hamming models. No longer-length theorem is required for this precisely motivated finite optimum.

final_claim: Among GC-content-two DNA four-mers, closed under Watson–Crick reverse-complement, disallowing self-complements and with disjoint length-three one-deletion shadows, largest code has 14 words; there are 20 labeled optima in four symmetry orbits 4,4,4,8.
limitations: Only exactly four bases per codeword, GC=2 and one deletion; no assertion for biochemistry or longer block lengths.
Priority of previously unindexed equality censuses remains open.
